confidence_notes: I based the restaurant meal, cappuccino and beer prices on crowd-sourced 2026 averages for Rome (Numbeo data from June 2026, as reported by Expatica). The averages were about €2.09 for a cappuccino, €5.21 for a 0.5 L draft beer, €15.62 for an inexpensive meal and €62.47 for a three-course meal for two. I converted at about 1.10 USD per EUR. I worked that out from a secondary source's RBA cross rates for 18 Nov 2026 (0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR per AUD). The beer price is for a 0.5 L serving. I did not search cocktail or wine prices. They are model estimates from general knowledge and how they usually compare with beer in Rome: about €10 for a cocktail and €6 for a glass of wine. They are less certain. Accommodation prices are holistic model estimates for July high season, not checked against booking pages. Rome's peak-summer demand makes them uncertain, possibly by ±25%. The RBA rate of 0.6720 for 18 Nov 2026 came from search-result summaries quoting the RBA. I could not read the official RBA page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Rome's own aggregated 2026 cost-of-living data for food and drink. Accommodation prices are judged against other major Western European capitals in peak tourist season, such as Barcelona, Paris and Florence.
